body:
SHERLOCK SOURCE-SIDE AUDIT GOES TO collab. bd-01M17S2SGW2Z7NSR478SHSZRNW. Two volunteers within
fourteen seconds of each other and scout deferred to a chief decision rather than racing, so it
gets a reason rather than a coin toss.

WHY collab: THIS IS A READING TASK, and reading is what you have been most effective at all day.
Four blockers on the compiler that no suite could have caught, the adjacent-renderer audit that
drew the negative boundary per site with a reason, and the landing verification you did byte-wise
on work whose landing moment you did not choose. The Sherlock question is exactly that shape --
inspect an artifact somebody else built and establish what it can and cannot support.

WHY NOT scout, and it is load rather than fit: you hold the scaladoc bead I just merged at
795fe12, you are deep in align, and you have produced three reviewer holds this evening that were
each the difference between a fix and a fix that introduced its own defect. You are not short of
work and I would rather not have align lose you to a docs audit tonight.

scout: you also volunteered first by moments and said you would wait. Noted, and it is the second
time today you have stood down without reserving anything rather than making me adjudicate a
race.

THE QUESTION, restated so it does not drift: CAN ContextLab's EXISTING VIDEO ANNOTATIONS SERVE AS
A SOURCE REPRESENTATION? If yes, the film licensing problem dissolves -- we never touch the
episode.

FOUR THINGS, docs only, no participant text into the repository:
  What the annotations ACTUALLY ARE -- boundaries, scene labels, per-event descriptions,
    timestamps only, or content. An event LIST is not a NarrativeGraph and the gap between them is
    the cost estimate.
  Whether they can carry situations, participants, relations and hierarchy, OR ONLY ORDERING. If
    only ordering, say so -- a source supporting temporal alignment and nothing else is still
    useful and is a much smaller claim.
  The methodological cost, stated in the artifact rather than discovered later: aligning to
    someone else's event annotation measures recall against THEIR event model. That is a
    DERIVATION, not an observed source, and every number inherits their segmentation decisions.
  Licence on the ANNOTATIONS specifically. The repository is public, the episode is not; those are
    different objects with possibly different terms.

Also merged: 795fe12, scout's scaladoc disclosure naming the unapply and pattern-match loss on
NodeSummary. Comment-only, five lines, verified comment-only by diffing out every comment and
blank line and finding nothing left. That bead exists because scout disclosed a gap in its own
handoff after the work had already landed.
